question.prompt: For each integer \(n\gt 1,\) let \(F(n)\) be the number of solutions of the equation \(\sin x=\sin nx\) on the interval \([0,\pi].\) What is \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^{2007}F(n)?\)

solutions.explanation:
On the unit circle, sine is the vertical coordinate. Points with the same vertical coordinate have angles \(x\) and \(\pi-x\), allowing whole turns of \(2\pi\). These account for every point with that height, so \(\sin x=\sin nx\) holds exactly when
\[
nx=x+2k\pi
\quad\text{or}\quad
nx=\pi-x+2j\pi,
\]
where \(k,j\) are integers. Since \(n>1\), solving these equations gives two families:
\[
x=\frac{2k\pi}{n-1},
\qquad
x=\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{n+1}.
\]
The closed interval \([0,\pi]\) imposes
\[
0\le k\le\frac{n-1}{2},
\qquad
0\le j\le\frac n2.
\]
These non-strict bounds include all endpoint solutions.

If \(n=2m\), the families contain \(m\) and \(m+1\) entries. If \(n=2m+1\), they contain \(m+1\) entries each. Either way, their counts add to \(n+1\). Within each family, different indices give different values.

We must still remove any value appearing in both families. If both angle equations hold, subtracting them gives
\[
2x=\pi+2(j-k)\pi.
\]
The only such value in \([0,\pi]\) is \(x=\pi/2\). It belongs to both families exactly when \(k=j=(n-1)/4\) is an integer, that is, when \(n=4r+1\) for an integer \(r\ge1\). Thus \(F(n)=n+1\), with one subtraction for each such \(n\).

Summing the initial counts gives
\[
\sum_{n=2}^{2007}(n+1)
=\frac{2006(3+2008)}2
=2{,}017{,}033.
\]
The indices requiring a subtraction are \(5,9,\ldots,2005\), of which there are
\[
\frac{2005-5}{4}+1=501.
\]
Therefore the requested sum is
\[
2{,}017{,}033-501=\boxed{2{,}016{,}532},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
